# Measured Split Rule for Two-Path Co-Termination in a Sovereign Swarm

## 1. Model (every symbol is a measurement)

Two resource paths **P** and **H** carry backlogs of work. The swarm has **N** sovereign agents, no leader. Assign `n_P` agents to P and `n_H = N − n_P` to H. Define the split as the agent-count ratio:

```
q ≡ n_P / n_H
```

| Symbol | Meaning | How it is measured |
|---|---|---|
| `B_P`, `B_H` | Backlog: remaining work units on each path | Counter-derived only: queued + incomplete items (bytes unacked + bytes queued for streams). Decremented on commit events, incremented on arrival. Never taken from a plan. |
| `r_P`, `r_H` | Per-agent drain rate (work units / agent / second) | `r̂_i = EWMA_τ(committed work in window) / (active agents × window)`, τ = 10 s |
| `m` | Skew multiplier | `m = r̂_H / r̂_P`, recomputed every tick |
| `Ŝ_P`, `Ŝ_H` | Saturation ceiling per path (aggregate goodput plateau) | Measured by periodic load-step probe: raise load until goodput flattens; record the plateau |

Completion times under linear drain:

```
T_P = B_P / (n_P · r_P)        T_H = B_H / (n_H · r_H)
```

## 2. Derivation — three lines, exact

Co-termination means `T_P = T_H`:

```
B_P / (n_P r_P) = B_H / (n_H r_H)
⟹  n_P / n_H = (r_H / r_P) · (B_P / B_H)
⟹  q* = m · B_P / B_H,     m ≡ r_H / r_P        ∎
```

Equivalent fractional form (if you allocate a share instead of a ratio):

```
f*_P = q* / (1 + q*) = m·B_P / (m·B_P + B_H)
```

Scale-invariance: only the *ratios* `B_P/B_H` and `r_H/r_P` enter. Multiplying both backlogs by any constant leaves `q*` unchanged.

**Why m is measured-not-guessed:** `m` is defined as the ratio of two measured drain rates. Every asymmetry the model doesn't name explicitly — protocol overhead, retry rate, link quality, verification cost per path — is absorbed into `r̂_P` and `r̂_H` automatically, because those are observed outputs, not modeled inputs. `m` is therefore a *sufficient statistic* for unknown path asymmetry under linear drain. Nothing is assumed about *why* the paths differ; only *how much* they differ, which is read off counters.

Sign convention: `m > 1` ⟺ P drains slower per agent (`r_P < r_H`) ⟺ P needs more than its raw backlog share.

## 3. Closed-form decision rule (full algorithm)

Executed every tick Δt = 1 s from fresh measurements:

```
INPUT : B_P, B_H, r̂_P, r̂_H, Ŝ_P, Ŝ_H, N, λ_P, λ_H   (all measured)

1. m_raw = r̂_H / r̂_P
2. if commits_in_window < 30 on either path:
       m = m_frozen (last trusted value);  deadband ×2   # insufficient data: don't chase noise
   else:
       m = clamp(m_raw, 0.25, 4.0)

3. # Streaming stability floor (only if arrivals λ_i > 0):
   n_P_min = ceil(λ_P / r̂_P);   n_H_min = ceil(λ_H / r̂_H)
   S = N − n_P_min − n_H_min                          # discretionary surplus

4. q* = m · B_P / B_H                                # the split
   n_P* = n_P_min + round( S · q* / (1 + q*) )
   n_H* = N − n_P*

5. # Saturation clamp:
   if n_P* · r̂_P > Ŝ_P:  n_P* = floor(Ŝ_P / r̂_P);  n_H* = N − n_P*
   if n_H* · r̂_H > Ŝ_H:  n_H* = floor(Ŝ_H / r̂_H);  n_P* = N − n_H*

6. # Degenerate branch (co-termination infeasible):
   if T̂_P(n_P*) ≠ T̂_H(n_H*) after clamping:
       rule degrades to minimize-max-finish: saturate BOTH paths
       (n_P = floor(Ŝ_P/r̂_P), n_H = N − n_P)         # fastest possible, gap unavoidable

7. # Hysteresis (anti-thrash, protects flock alignment):
   if |n_P_current − n_P*| ≥ max(1, ceil(0.05·N)):
       migrate μ = max(1, ceil(0.02·N)) agents per tick toward n_P*

8. # Self-verification:
   if |T̂_P − T̂_H| / max(T̂_P, T̂_H) > 0.05 for 3 consecutive ticks:
       linear-drain model is violated → switch to iterative mode:
       re-measure r̂_i at current n_i, recompute q*, repeat (fixed-point iteration;
       converges because T_P − T_H is strictly decreasing in n_P — see §5)
```

Integer-rounding residual: with N agents the achievable gap is `O(1/N)` relative — co-termination is enforced to tolerance `ε_T = 5%`, which is the honest meaning of "finish together" with discrete agents.

## 4. Worked example (numbers close exactly)

N = 100. Measured: `B_P = 12 000`, `B_H = 5 000` units; `r̂_P = 40`, `r̂_H = 25` u/agent/s.

```
m  = 25/40 = 0.625
q* = 0.625 × 12000/5000 = 1.5
n_P* = 100 × 1.5/2.5 = 60,   n_H* = 40
```

Check: `T_P = 12000/(60·40) = 5.000 s`; `T_H = 5000/(40·25) = 5.000 s`. **Both finish at t = 5 s.** Interpretation: P holds 2.4× the backlog but drains 1.6× faster per agent, so it needs only 1.5× the agents — the multiplier `m` is exactly what corrects the naive backlog-proportional guess.

## 5. Sovereign enforcement — no leader required

Two equivalent mechanisms; pick one:

**(a) Price-migration dynamics (pure flock, zero consensus rounds).** Each agent locally computes `T̂_P`, `T̂_H` from its own estimates and migrates to the *slower* path with logistic probability `p = σ(β·(T_slow − T_fast))`. At stationarity, net flux between paths is zero ⟺ expected finish times equal ⟺ `T_P = T_H`. The flock's local alignment-type rule *is* the equalizer; the balanced split `q*` emerges as the unique stable fixed point. Global stability: `F(n_P) = T_P(n_P) − T_H(N−n_P)` is continuous, strictly decreasing (`dT_P/dn_P < 0`, `dT_H/dn_P > 0`), with `F(0) > 0`, `F(N) < 0` ⟹ unique root, globally attracting.

**(b) Gossip consensus on the four scalars.** Agents exchange `(B, r)` views with k neighbors every Δt_gossip and average (median-of-neighbors, not mean, for byzantine robustness). Standard average-consensus convergence drives all agents' estimates to the graph aggregate; since `q*` is a pure function of four scalars, all agents then compute an identical `q*` with no coordinator. Accept any single backlog delta > threshold only with 2f+1 matching witnesses; rate-limit per-tick belief revision to bound one faulty node's influence.

## 6. Guards and edge cases (exact behavior)

- **`B_H = 0`:** `q*` diverges ⟹ assign all agents to P, except hold `n_H = ceil(λ_H/r̂_H)` if H receives arrivals.
- **Starved window (<30 commits):** freeze `m`, double the deadband, flag low-confidence. Never substitute a guessed `m`.
- **Post-hoc tuning ban:** τ = 10 s, φ = 0.05, ν = 0.02, ε_T = 5%, m-clamp [0.25, 4], k = 3 are fixed *a priori*. Adjusting them after seeing outcomes reintroduces guessing through the back door.
- **Auditability:** log `(B_P, B_H, r̂_P, r̂_H, m, q*, n_P, T̂_P, T̂_H)` each tick. "Measured-not-guessed" is operationalized as: every decision is reproducible from the logged counters alone.

**Summary rule:** `q* = (r̂_H/r̂_P) · (B_P/B_H)`, applied with stability floors, saturation clamps, and a 5% deadband — three measured quantities, one division, co-termination guaranteed to integer resolution whenever the uncapped fixed point exists.
reasoning:
Let me parse this problem carefully. The user is asking about a "measured split q* = m·B_P/B_H" that makes two resource paths finish together, in the context of "sovereign swarm / flock consensus."

This appears to be about a swarm/flock consensus system where:
- There are two resource paths (two work streams / two sub-swarms) that need to finish at the same time
- q* is the optimal split ratio of resources between them
- B_P and B_H appear to be bandwidth/capacity terms — perhaps "B_P" = path/bandwidth for one resource (P), "B_H" = bandwidth for another (H)
- m is some multiplier or measured factor
- The goal: make both paths finish together (synchronize completion)

The user wants:
1. Measured signals (not guessed) — i.e., what telemetry/measurements feed into this
2. A closed-form decision rule — an exact formula

Let me think about what makes two paths finish together.

Setup: Two paths, P and H (maybe "primary" and "helper", or "payload" and "housekeeping", or in flock terms maybe "path" and "hub"). Each has a workload W_P and W_H (work to do), and each gets allocated resources. The split is q = fraction going to P vs H, or a ratio.

If we allocate resources proportionally to work, both finish simultaneously. Classic result: to equalize completion times T_P = T_H, you need allocation proportional to remaining work divided by service rate.

Let me formalize:

Path P has remaining work W_P (e.g., bytes to move, tasks to complete). Path H has W_H.
Resource capacities: B_P = bandwidth available on path P, B_H = bandwidth available on path H.
Time to finish if fully dedicated: T_P = W_P/B_P, T_H = W_H/B_H.

Now we have a shared pool of agents/resources (the swarm), total capacity C, and we split it: fraction q goes to path P, (1−q) to path H. Then:

T_P(q) = W_P / (q·C)
T_H(q) = W_H / ((1−q)·C)

Setting T_P = T_H:
W_P/q = W_H/(1−q)
W_P(1−q) = W_H·q
W_P − W_P·q = W_H·q
q(W_P + W_H) = W_P
q* = W_P/(W_P + W_H)

That's the classic proportional-share rule. But the problem states q* = m·B_P/B_H. So the split involves the ratio of bandwidths times a multiplier m.

Hmm. Let me reconsider. Maybe the setup is different: the paths themselves have intrinsic bandwidths B_P and B_H (like network links), and the swarm must decide how many agents m to send down... Actually "m" might be the number of agents/members assigned.

Alternative reading: q* = m·(B_P/B_H) where m is a measured correction factor. The naive guess would be q = B_P/B_H (split proportional to link capacity), but measurement shows you need multiplier m ≠ 1 because of overheads, latency differences, queueing, etc.

So the structure of the answer should be:

1. Define the two paths and their completion-time models with measured parameters.
2. Derive the closed form: finish-together condition ⇒ q* formula.
3. Show that q* = m·B_P/B_H emerges naturally, with m being a measured composite of overheads (e.g., m = (1+ε_P)/(1+ε_H) · something).
4. List the exact measured signals needed: per-path throughput measurements, RTT, queue depth, work remaining, etc.
5. Give the decision rule as a closed-form inequality/equality with hysteresis band for stability (to avoid thrashing).

Let me build a concrete model grounded in real swarm/flock consensus mechanics.

Model: Sovereign swarm = N autonomous agents, no central controller; consensus via local rules (flock: separation/alignment/cohesion analogs → here: agreement on task allocation via gossip/voting). Two resource paths P and H must complete their workloads by the same deadline (finish together). The swarm allocates a fraction q of its members (or bandwidth share) to path P.

Measured signals (all measurable, no guessing):

1. Per-path goodput: G_P, G_H — measured completed-work-per-second over a sliding window τ (e.g., EWMA with time constant τ). Units: work-units/sec.
2. Remaining work: Ŵ_P, Ŵ_H — measured from progress counters (bytes left, tasks left), not estimated from plans.
3. Link/base capacities: B_P, B_H — measured maximum sustainable rate per agent on each path (calibration probes or observed peak under saturation).
4. Overhead factors: ε_P, ε_H — measured ratio of useful work to total work (retransmits, retries, coordination cost). Measured as 1 − (wasted/work_total).
5. Queue/backlog: Q_P, Q_H — current unprocessed items in each path's inbound buffer.
6. Arrival rates (if streaming): λ_P, λ_H — new work arriving per second.

Completion time model for path i:
T_i = (Q_i + Ŵ_i) / (n_i · g_i)

where n_i = number of agents on path i, g_i = per-agent goodput on path i.

Per-agent goodput relates to base capacity: g_i = B_i·η_i where η_i ∈ (0,1] is measured efficiency (overhead factor).

Finish-together condition:
(Q_P + Ŵ_P)/(q·N·B_P·η_P) = (Q_H + Ŵ_H)/((1−q)·N·B_H·η_H)

Solve for q:
Let W̃_P = Q_P + Ŵ_P (total pending work on P), W̃_H = Q_H + Ŵ_H.

W̃_P·(1−q)·B_H·η_H = W̃_H·q·B_P·η_P
W̃_P·B_H·η_H − q·W̃_P·B_H·η_H = q·W̃_H·B_P·η_P
W̃_P·B_H·η_H = q·(W̃_P·B_H·η_H + W̃_H·B_P·η_P)
q* = W̃_P·B_H·η_H / (W̃_P·B_H·η_H + W̃_H·B_P·η_P)

Divide numerator and denominator by B_H·η_H... let me get it into the form m·B_P/B_H.

q* = [W̃_P·B_H·η_H] / [W̃_P·B_H·η_H + W̃_H·B_P·η_P]

Divide num and denom by (W̃_P·B_H·η_H):
q* = 1 / (1 + (W̃_H/W̃_P)·(B_P·η_P)/(B_H·η_H))

Hmm, that's 1/(1+r) form. To express as m·B_P/B_H:

q*/(1−q*) = (W̃_P·η_H)/(W̃_H·η_P) · (B_H/B_P)

So odds form: q*/(1−q*) = m'·(B_H/B_P) where m' = (W̃_P·η_H)/(W̃_H·η_P).

Alternatively solve directly for q* = m·B_P/B_H form. Let's see:

From q*/(1−q*) = K, we get q* = K/(1+K).

With K = (W̃_P·η_H·B_H)/(W̃_H·η_P·B_P).

Then q* = (W̃_P·η_H·B_H) / (W̃_P·η_H·B_H + W̃_H·η_P·B_P).

To write q* = m·B_P/B_H exactly, we'd need... hmm, that doesn't naturally give B_P/B_H in numerator unless the workloads are related differently.

Maybe I'm overcomplicating. Perhaps the intended model: the split q is the number of agents m sent to path P relative to path H, and the natural balance point is when agents-per-bandwidth equalizes. Let me think again.

Alternative interpretation: q = m·B_P/B_H where:
- B_P, B_H are measured bottleneck bandwidths of the two paths,
- m is the measured "drift" or "skew" multiplier capturing how much faster one path completes per unit bandwidth due to differing work sizes.

Actually, maybe simpler: the user gives the target form q* = m·B_P/B_H and wants us to (a) define what m is measurably, (b) derive why that form is correct, (c) give the decision rule using it.

Let me construct the derivation so that q* = m·B_P/B_H falls out cleanly.

Suppose the swarm splits N agents: m agents to path P, and the rest scale so that the ratio of agents is q = n_P/n_H. For both paths to finish together:

T_P = W̃_P/(n_P·b_P) = T_H = W̃_H/(n_H·b_H)

where b_i = per-agent effective rate on path i = B_i·η_i (B_i = measured per-agent line rate, η_i = measured efficiency).

n_P/n_H = (W̃_P·b_H)/(W̃_H·b_P) = (W̃_P·η_H·B_H)/(W̃_H·η_P·B_P)

Still B_H/B_P in the ratio. Hmm.

Unless... the workloads themselves scale with bandwidth. E.g., path P carries payload whose volume is proportional to B_P (you send as much as the pipe allows), and similarly for H. Then W̃_P ∝ B_P·t_remaining, and:

n_P/n_H = (B_P·η_H·B_H)/(B_H·η_P·B_P) = η_H/η_P.

Nope, bandwidth cancels.

Try yet another framing: q is the fraction of a single shared channel/time-slot given to P. The completion condition with a shared pipe of capacity C:

Path P needs W_P work; gets share q·C but only achieves efficiency e_P(q) (efficiency may depend on share due to protocol overheads, e.g., TCP-like behavior, or coordination cost growing with sub-swarm size).

T_P = W_P/(q·C·e_P), T_H = W_H/((1−q)·C·e_H)

Equalize: q/(1−q) = (W_P·e_H)/(W_H·e_P)... same structure.

OK here's another thought: maybe B_P and B_H aren't bandwidths of the paths but "backlogs": B_P = backlog on path P, B_H = backlog on path H! That makes much more sense for the formula q* = m·B_P/B_H!

If B_P = backlog (remaining work) on path P and B_H = backlog on path H, then the classic finish-together split is:

q* = B_P/(B_P + B_H) — split proportional to backlog.

And m·B_P/B_H... hmm, still not quite. Unless q is defined as the ratio rather than fraction.

Wait — maybe q is defined as the split RATIO n_P/n_H (not fraction), and the finish-together condition gives:

n_P/n_H = (B_P·v_H)/(B_H·v_P)

where v_i = per-agent velocity/rate on path i. If per-agent rates are equal (homogeneous swarm, v_P = v_H = v), then:

q* = n_P/n_H = B_P/B_H.

And with heterogeneous rates or overheads, q* = m·B_P/B_H where m = v_H/v_P = measured relative speed factor. YES. This is clean.

So the model:
- Two resource paths P and H, backlogs B_P and B_H (measured remaining work units).
- Swarm assigns agents at ratio q = n_P/n_H.
- Per-agent effective completion rates r_P and r_H (measured goodput per agent on each path).
- Completion times: T_P = B_P/(n_P·r_P), T_H = B_H/(n_H·r_H).
- Finish together ⟺ T_P = T_H ⟺ n_P/n_H = (B_P·r_H)/(B_H·r_P).
- Define m = r_H/r_P (measured speed-ratio correction). Then q* = m·B_P/B_H. ✓

This matches the requested form exactly. And m is measured, not guessed: m = r̂_H/r̂_P from sliding-window goodput measurements.

But wait — there's subtlety: r_P itself may depend on n_P (congestion/diminishing returns per path: more agents on one path → contention → lower per-agent rate). Then the fixed point shifts. Let me handle that too, since a rigorous answer should address it.

Model with congestion: r_P(n_P) = r_P⁰·f(n_P) where f is decreasing, e.g., f(n) = 1/(1+n/K) (processor-sharing-like) or f(n) = min(1, C_path/(n·r⁰)) (hard capacity cap). The hard cap version is very concrete:

Each path has a measured saturation capacity S_P, S_H (max aggregate goodput, measured by load-stepping until goodput flattens). Then:

T_P = max(B_P/(n_P·r_P⁰), B_P/S_P) — actually T_P = B_P/min(n_P·r_P⁰, S_P).

Finish-together with caps: choose n_P, n_H such that B_P/(n_P·r_P⁰) = B_H/(n_H·r_H⁰) AND n_P·r_P⁰ ≤ S_P, n_H·r_H⁰ ≤ S_H. If unconstrained solution violates a cap, clamp: saturate the capped path at S_i and give all remaining agents to the other path, then re-check whether the other path now finishes earlier — if so, the best you can do is bounded by the saturated path (can't finish together; finish as early as possible = saturate both).

Also dynamic version: backlogs drain over time, arrivals add work. The decision rule should be receded-horizon: recompute q* every control tick Δt from fresh measurements. Add hysteresis: only rebalance when |q_meas − q*| > δ (deadband) to prevent oscillation/thrashing in the flock (this matters for flock consensus stability — constant reshuffling destroys alignment).

Consensus angle ("sovereign swarm / flock"): how do decentralized agents agree on q without a leader? Options:
- Each agent measures local view of B_P, B_H, r_P, r_H via gossip; converges to same q* if measurements converge (average consensus on the four signals).
- Or: market/auction-based: paths post "urgency price" π_i = T_i (predicted finish time); agents migrate toward the slower path (higher T_i) until prices equalize — this is a distributed equalization dynamics: dn_P/dt ∝ (T_H − T_P). At equilibrium T_P = T_H, which is exactly the finish-together condition. Nice: the flock's alignment rule IS the equalizer. The stable fixed point of "move toward the lagging path" is the balanced split.

Stability of that migration dynamics: d(T_P − T_H)/d(n_P) < 0 required. Check: T_P = B_P/(n_P r_P), increasing n_P decreases T_P; also decreases n_H hence increases T_H. So T_P − T_H strictly decreasing in n_P ⇒ unique fixed point ⇒ globally stable (for the uncapped case). Good, can state that.

Now the measured signals list — be exact:

Signal definitions (each with estimator):
1. B_P, B_H — backlog: measured remaining work units on each path. Estimator: sum over queued/incomplete items; for byte-streams, bytes_unacked + bytes_queued. Update: decrement on commit events, increment on arrival. No estimation from plans — counter-derived only.
2. r_P, r_H — per-agent drain rate: measured goodput per active agent. Estimator: r̂_i = EWMA_τ(work committed in window)/(active_agents × window). Use exponentially weighted moving average with half-life h (pick h ≈ 2–5× typical inter-commit interval, or state τ = 10 s as concrete default).
3. m = r̂_H/r̂_P — the skew multiplier. Recomputed each tick. Guard: clamp m to [m_min, m_max] = [0.25, 4] (or [1/κ, κ]) when sample count below threshold n_min (e.g., <30 commits in window) — fall back to m=1 with wide deadband (insufficient data ⇒ don't chase noise).
4. Optional second-order signals: saturation caps S_P, S_H (measured via periodic probe: briefly overload path, read plateau); arrival rates λ_P, λ_H (measured arrival counter derivative) for the streaming variant.

Closed-form decision rule:

Given measurements at tick t: B_P(t), B_H(t), r̂_P(t), r̂_H(t):

q*(t) = (r̂_H(t)/r̂_P(t)) · B_P(t)/B_H(t)   … target agent-count ratio n_P/n_H.

Convert to integer assignment with N total agents:
n_P* = round(N · q*/(1+q*)), n_H* = N − n_P*.

Rebalance trigger (hysteresis): migrate only if |n_P^current − n_P*| ≥ θ, with θ = max(1, ⌈φN⌉), φ ≈ 0.05–0.1. Migration rate limited: move μ = max(1, ⌈νN⌉) agents per tick, ν ≈ 0.02, to keep flock coherence (alignment cost of mass migration).

Feasibility clamps:
- If n_P*·r̂_P > Ŝ_P (would exceed measured saturation), set n_P ← ⌊Ŝ_P/r̂_P⌋, dump remainder to H.
- Post-clamp check: if T_P(clamped) < T_H, the pair cannot finish together this horizon; rule becomes "minimize max T_i" = saturate both: n_P = ⌊Ŝ_P/r̂_P⌋, n_H = N − n_P (and vice versa). State this explicitly as the degenerate branch.

Streaming/steady-state variant (arrivals λ_P, λ_H): replace backlog B_i with effective load L_i = B_i + λ_i·T̄ where T̄ is the horizon; or better, use the fluid condition: for both queues to be stable and finish together, need n_P·r_P ≥ λ_P and n_H·r_H ≥ λ_H first (stability constraints), then split surplus proportionally to backlog. Closed form: 
n_P^min = λ_P/r_P, n_H^min = λ_H/r_H. Surplus N' = N − n_P^min − n_H^min distributed as q_surplus = m·B_P/B_H. Final n_P = n_P^min + N'·q*/(1+q*). This is the complete rule for the general case. Good—include it.

Derivation to show (compact but complete):
T_P = B_P/(n_P r_P), T_H = B_H/(n_H r_H). Set equal:
B_P r_H n_H = B_H r_P n_P ⇒ n_P/n_H = (r_H/r_P)(B_P/B_H) = m·B_P/B_H. QED. One line, exact.

Why measured-not-guessed: every symbol is a counter or a ratio of counters over a window; nothing comes from a plan or a guess. m absorbs ALL unmodeled asymmetry (per-path protocol overhead, retry rates, terrain/link quality, verification cost differences) because it's defined as the ratio of measured drain rates — any physics not captured shows up in r̂ automatically. That's the key epistemic point: m is a sufficient statistic for unknown path asymmetry under the linear-drain model. Caveat honestly: if drain is nonlinear in n (contention), m becomes n-dependent; handle via the saturation clamp + local linearization: measure r̂_i at current n_i, iterate the fixed point (one Newton step per tick suffices since contraction holds — can state contraction: |d(T_P−T_H)/dn_P| bounded away from 0).

Flock-consensus implementation (sovereign = no leader):
- Each agent i keeps local estimates via gossip: periodically (every Δt_gossip) exchange (B_i^view, r_i^view) with k neighbors; update own estimate as weighted average (weight ∝ recency). Consensus convergence: standard average-consensus guarantees all agents' estimates converge to graph-mean of measurements; since q* is a function of the four scalars, all agents compute identical q* once estimates agree within tolerance. Alternatively, avoid global agreement entirely: use the price-dynamics migration rule — each agent compares local T̂_P vs T̂_H and defects to the slower path with probability p = σ(β(T_slow − T_fast)) (logistic). Equilibrium distribution satisfies detailed balance at T_P = T_H ⇒ same fixed point, reached without any explicit consensus round.
